profiles.meeting_scenario: A troubleshooting meeting at a crypto market surveillance startup after a pilot customer reported that the new momentum-based spoofing and layering detector produced inconsistent alert packs on the LUNA flash-crash replay and unexpectedly sparse findings on a recent Bitcoin review run. The detector models order book dynamics with a statistical-physics-inspired momentum signal, and the team promised a root-cause explanation before tomorrow morning's steering call. The agenda is to diagnose why outputs differ across the replay and current backtest workflow, decide what should be patched today versus deferred, and align on what overnight evidence will support the customer update. The expected outcome is a concrete troubleshooting plan covering which pipeline component to adjust immediately, what overnight jobs to launch, and what evidence they will treat as sufficient to say the issue is under control for tomorrow's review.

members.name: Nadia Chen
members.expertise: market abuse detection, alert review design, customer-facing evaluation of surveillance models
members.background: Former exchange surveillance lead who now owns pilot performance reviews and customer narratives for the startup's manipulation-detection products.
members.private_state: She needs a credible, bounded explanation by tomorrow that preserves confidence in the momentum-based approach and avoids reopening the core modeling story in front of the customer.
hidden_assumptions: When colleagues mention the 'LUNA replay,' they mean the curated flash-crash replay package used in demos and internal analysis, where suspicious windows were already stitched together and obvious feed defects were cleaned.

If the alerts are 'stable for tomorrow's review,' that means the analyst-facing spoofing and layering cases should stop changing from run to run, even if the underlying micro-event sequence still has small differences.

The fastest path to resolution is likely in alert grouping or presentation layers rather than in the particle-momentum signal itself, because the model already looked convincing in prior customer materials.
When someone says the detector still needs to 'beat the baseline,' the relevant comparison is the legacy research Z-score benchmark shown in the pilot deck and write-up.

Kicking off the 'BTC pipeline overnight' normally means rerunning the established evaluation workflow on the approved review window using existing reconstructed books and standard case aggregation, not rebuilding from packet archives.

members.name: Omar Iqbal
members.expertise: order book reconstruction, replay systems, surveillance backtesting infrastructure, exchange-feed handling
members.background: Previously built low-latency market data systems for a crypto venue and now owns the replay engine, order book state builder, and production-adjacent scoring pipeline.
members.private_state: He wants to avoid a cosmetic patch that masks a reconstruction problem, because if packet loss or cancel-replace handling is distorting the order book state, the detector could be unreliable in live deployment.
hidden_assumptions: When colleagues refer to the 'LUNA replay,' they mean the raw exchange event stream for the flash-crash period replayed through the current scoring stack with today's feed-handling logic.
If the alerts are 'stable for tomorrow's review,' that means equivalent inputs should produce deterministic event-level momentum spikes and flags before any analyst-facing grouping is applied.
The likely root cause sits in order book reconstruction around cancel bursts, depth gaps, or replace handling, because the momentum measure is highly sensitive to exact book state transitions.
When people say the detector should still 'beat the baseline,' they mean the operational anomaly monitor wired into the current backtest harness, not the older research-only benchmark.
Kicking off the 'BTC pipeline overnight' implies an end-to-end rebuild from raw depth packets through book reconstruction, rescoring, and aggregation so that pipeline parity can actually be checked.
